5.34.betting_forecast: 7/2 Shutfrontdoor, 4/1 Hidden Fortune, Sorgean, 5/1 Flash Bardot, 11/2 Secret Des Lune, 6/1 Rock Sensation, 10/1 Diamond
5.34.spotlight_verdict: Shutfrontdoor was a clear second at Plumpton last month and is not opposed lightly but FLASH BARDOT shaped well when third on last month's stable/hurdle debut at Haydock, and her Flat ability offers significant hope she can build on that performance. Bumper winners Secret Des Lune and Sorgean can also feature.[Chris Wilson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Runner-up on last year's Irish point debut and made the frame in all three subsequent bumpers; no match for clear winner when second at Kelso (good to soft) in March but still enters calculations on hurdle debut.

Useful over middle distances on the Flat (five wins) and made promising stable/hurdle debut when third at Haydock (1m7f, good) last month; that run came after a layoff and she'll be dangerous if it brought her on.
Irish point winner who came second in two five-runner bumpers last season (good to soft/good); switches to hurdling with potential but may not be seen to best effect until tackling longer trips.
Not disgraced when midfield at Chepstow (2m, good) last month but the value of that form is open to question and others in this line-up have much stronger claims.

Won good-ground Southwell bumper for Ben Pauling in spring 2025 and made the frame in soft-ground Listed event at Cheltenham in November but didn't get far on hurdling debut in December and was remote when third at Lingfield (2m3f, good to soft) later that month; makes stable debut after a break and with a point to prove.
Tailed off in both bumpers and unseated her rider after trying to refuse at second flight on hurdle debut; cannot be recommended.

Delivered on earlier promise when battling well to win five-runner Plumpton bumper (good to soft) in March; likely to encounter faster ground on this hurdling debut but ought to play a significant role.
Bumper winner; well held when falling heavily on hurdle debut in December but returned from break with two pretty good seconds towards end of last season (both 2m, good); probably won't be far away.
horses.trainer: J Hinds, A Head & G L Moore G & J Moore

horses.spotlight_comment: Joined Harry Fry after going close in an Irish point in November and made winning rules debut in five-runner Wincanton bumper (good) last month; that form isn't anything to get too excited about but she should have more to offer over hurdles.
Not beaten far when eighth of 12 in good-ground Newton Abbot bumper last month, her second start, but still makes only limited appeal on this hurdling debut.

6.10.betting_forecast: 15/8 Oakley, 5/1 Motazzen, Taritino, 11/2 Bel Ombre, 6/1 Sun Joy, 12/1 Khalk'Eau Spigao, 16/1 Belgarum, Hiconic.
6.10.spotlight_verdict: There is probably still more to come from newly hooded 6yo BEL OMBRE, who spoiled his chance by racing too freely at Perth last month but won with an indeterminate amount left in the tank on his handicap debut two starts ago. Oakley (second choice) sauntered to victory at Hereford last week and is slightly ahead of the handicapper under a penalty but it's hard to tell whether he'll be in the same mood again. Taritino is next on the list, while good market support will heighten interest in handicap debutant Khalk'eau Spigao.[Chris Wilson]

horses.spotlight_comment: No match for winner when second at Perth (2m4f, good; raced too freely) last month, after a break, but appeared to have quite a bit in hand when winning on handicap debut at Taunton (2m3f, good to soft) in January and can be dangerous if new hood helps him to relax.

Four-time chase winner who was out of sorts when last seen in the autumn, most recently when pulled up on return to hurdling; had another wind op (his fourth) during 168-day break; needs to get career back on track.
horses.trainer: Mrs G C Pritchard J Tizzard

horses.spotlight_comment: Came second off basement Flat mark on latest outing in January and is well handicapped for this return to hurdling but she's not as good as she was and has become inconsistent; others appeal more.
Showed nothing more than minor promise in his three qualifying races last season (2m-2m1f) and is 2lb out of the weights for this handicap debut but improvement is possible at some stage.
horses.trainer: D S Dennis & John Hw Finch C Gordon

horses.spotlight_comment: Four-time hurdle winner who rewarded good market support and showed career-best form when drawing clear to score by 10l here (2m5f, good to soft) in March; 8lb rise asks a fair bit of him but the forecast faster ground should not be a problem.
horses.trainer: Carol & Chris Jackson & Henrietta Knight Henrietta Knight

horses.spotlight_comment: 2-7 for current stable since the autumn, the latter win gained easily by over 8l at Hereford (2m3f, good) nine days ago; not always one to rely upon heavily but has obvious claims under 7lb penalty.
horses.trainer: Mrs C Williams Mrs C Williams

horses.spotlight_comment: Back in prime form when last seen in the autumn, winning at Ludlow before running well in defeat at Kempton (also 2m5f, good); contender if ready to roll after six-month break.
horses.trainer: The Salmon Spray Partnership B Pauling
horses.breeding: b m Sixties Icon - Hi Note

horses.spotlight_comment: Looked as good as ever when winning readily by 7l at favourite track Taunton (2m3f, good) three weeks ago and is now 3-19 over hurdles; 7lb higher here but still respected in current mood.

6.40.betting_forecast: 2/1 Ballyfinn, 5/2 Thickthorn Tom, 4/1 Misteroddsocks, 7/1 Lunar Ocean, 8/1 All Authorized, 16/1 Jaffa Cake, 20/1 Lord Maher.
6.40.spotlight_verdict: Ballyfinn and MISTERODDSOCKS (nap) won at this track last time out and the latter gets the nod having done it over this trip. Thickthorn Tom and Lunar Ocean also need considering.[Richard Russell]

horses.spotlight_comment: Course bumper and hurdle winner who won Plumpton handicap hurdle off 18lb higher last April; subsequent starts over fences didn't go well and he resumes chase career having been well held over hurdles on last three starts.
horses.trainer: S Packham & The Dubai Five G & J Moore

horses.spotlight_comment: Made the breakthrough on his fifth start over fences when scoring here (3m2f, good) last Wednesday; back down in trip under 7lb penalty but not fully exposed and looks a key player.

Favourite when runner-up on bumper debut but little to shout about over hurdles and beaten a long way on his chase debut over C&D (good) in this headgear combination three weeks ago; respected yard but he needs to show more.
horses.breeding: b g Order Of St George - Tetou

horses.spotlight_comment: Can make mistakes but mainly consistent over fences for this yard; pulled up at Warwick after an error last time but 2m and ground that was likely faster than good were probably not ideal; that brought his record to 0-18 but he's not ruled out in first-time blinkers back up in trip.

Had wind surgery before he cashed in on a falling mark to open account over C&D (good to soft) last month; up 5lb for that head success but recent form counts for plenty in this race and he's a big player.
horses.breeding: b g Walk In The Park - Fairy Hill

horses.spotlight_comment: Much the best of two chase starts when third of 11 at Exeter (3m, good to soft) in March; drops back in trip with a tongue-tie joining his cheekpieces; unexposed and he's respected for top yard.
horses.trainer: Kate Fisher & Sally Hall D Skelton

7.10.betting_forecast: 7/2 Jager Time, 6/1 Lady Henrietta, 13/2 Hurst Hill, 7/1 For Old Times Sake, Nelson Gate, Renoir, 8/1 Counteract, 10/1 Tell The
7.10.spotlight_verdict: Some of these remain unexposed and tricky to weigh up but the betting market is likely to reveal some clues. Jager Time was in good form when last seen in the autumn but it might be worth chancing the veteran COUNTERACT, who has an unusual profile but who ran better than his eventual 72l defeat might suggest here three weeks ago. That stable debut was his first run since 2023 and today's drop back in trip looks the right move. Hurst Hill also has possibilities.[Chris Wilson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Jumped left throughout and was beaten about 60l on recent handicap debut at Exeter (2m2f, good); this switch to a left-handed track is an obvious move but he needs to take a big step forward over the new trip.
horses.breeding: b g Masterstroke - The Prime Viper

horses.spotlight_comment: 0-6 over hurdles, having struggled in his last two handicaps (2m4f/2mf, good; warm favourite on first occasion); goes up in trip fitted with new tongue-tie; has a lot to prove but can't be written off yet.
Well beaten in first two handicaps (2m, soft/good; raced too freely last time); needs significant improvement but his pedigree and his Irish point form suggest this step up in trip will suit.
Just 1-17 over hurdles, the win gained at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) last summer, but she made a satisfactory reappearance last month and her current mark is workable; considered each-way.
horses.trainer: J H Young J S Mullins
horses.breeding: b m Arctic Cosmos - Nicat's Benefit

horses.spotlight_comment: Opened account over hurdles in 16-runner handicap at Huntingdon (3m1f, good) in November, his eighth attempt; not seen since and not sure to benefit from this drop back in trip but further progress is possible.
horses.breeding: ch g Champs Elysees - Ballyknock Mist

horses.spotlight_comment: Absent since struggling to cope with 3m on heavy ground in January but made all under Elliott England at Leicester (2m4f, heavy) in December and was placed on good ground in the autumn; no surprise if she features.
horses.breeding: b m Blue Bresil - Matrow's Lady

horses.spotlight_comment: Fair on the Flat; probably only sixth best on merit when fourth on handicap debut here (2m3f, good) three weeks ago but positives can be drawn from that performance and he might have more to offer over this longer trip.
horses.breeding: b g Australia - Star Of Spring

horses.spotlight_comment: Now 5lb lower than winning winning at Hereford (2m, good) in March 2025 but, following a break, could not justify favouritism when midfield at Stratford (2m2f; good; first run after wind op) last month; sports refitted cheekpieces and tries a new trip here; needs that recent run to have done him good.
Safely held in first two handicaps (2m3f/3m, good to soft) and absent since January but remains unexposed (particularly on good ground) and is worth a glance in the betting.
horses.breeding: b g Order Of St George - A Touch Of Sparkle

7.40.betting_forecast: 2/1 Grain Trade, 11/4 Saint Polo, 3/1 Model Approach, 9/1 Gone In Sixty, 10/1 Ballywood, 16/1 Daany, 20/1 Holy Legend, Millies
7.40.spotlight_verdict: Model Approach is ahead of his mark and the forecast sounder surface may help him show more on this third attempt over fences, while a clear round from Grain Trade would make him a danger to all. However, it's interesting that Jennie Candlish sends SAINT POLO on a fairly lengthy journey down to Fontwell and he gets the vote to make a successful chasing debut.[Richard Russell]

horses.spotlight_comment: Down to this mark when nearly winning for the first time in seven years at Huntingdon in March and a slightly lesser effort when third at Hereford (also 2m, good) came just one week later; not ruled out.
horses.trainer: Ms G Howell Ms G Howell

horses.spotlight_comment: Sole success came when wide-margin winner over hurdles at Fakenham just under one year ago but he's finished runner-up on 12 occasions, including five times in succession over fences between September and November; had wind surgery after heavy defeat over hurdles at Windsor over five months ago; market might guide on this return.
horses.trainer: Alex Hales Racing Club A Hales

horses.spotlight_comment: Ready win when beating seven others at Market Rasen (2m4f, good) on his second start chasing and looked set to defy a penalty when coming down at the last over C&D (good to soft) in October; jumping has been a bit of an issue since and he was narrowly in front when again coming down at the final fence back at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) one month ago; hood joins his regular tongue-tie.
horses.trainer: John Aprahamian & Co Ltd B Aprahamian

horses.spotlight_comment: Just four starts over fences and, after finishing tailed off in the first and refusing in the second, he showed he might be getting the hang of things when sixth of ten at Exeter (2m3f, good; weakened) last month; needs to take another step forward but that's not out of the question.
horses.breeding: b g Passing Glance - Holy Veil

horses.spotlight_comment: Course regular who has won twice (about 2m3f, good) and been placed on another four occasions from 15 visits; last won just over a year ago but looked to have something to offer when unseating four out in April and it was too far out to tell how she'd have fared when falling, again here, last time; 2lb wrong but she's not dismissed.

Beaten a combined 70l in two soft-ground starts over fences but he won his third hurdle race when picking up a 12-runner Ffos Las handicap (2m, good) off this mark nine days ago; 5lb well in on handicap marks if he can transfer that form to chasing and there should be no ground excuses this time.

Went close on handicap debut over hurdles at Sedgefield (2m4f) in March before solid third at Taunton (3m, also good) one month later; drops sharply back in trip with cheekpieces enlisted and he remains unexposed on this introduction to fences.
horses.breeding: b g Storm The Stars - Une Royal

8.10.betting_forecast: 11/4 Short Sell, 3/1 Red One, 5/1 Cameron De Fiacre, 6/1 Dernier Set, 8/1 Mysterland, 10/1 Norff N Sauff, 16/1 Horethorne, Lord
8.10.spotlight_verdict: This could be a good bumper for the time of year. Winning pointer Short Sell evidently has significant ability but preference is for Nicky Henderson's well-bred newcomer RED ONE. Jamie Snowden's newcomer Cameron De Fiacre also makes appeal on paper.[Chris Wilson]

horses.spotlight_comment: 45,000euros 2yo; third foal; half-brother to two French jumps winners; dam unraced half-sister to a French hurdle/chase winner; stable's excellent 27% strike-rate in bumpers brings him into the equation.
dam placed on Flat, closely related to 10.7f Listed Flat and hurdle winner Great Pretender; stable has 18% strike-rate in bumpers; no surprise if he features.
Out of a well-connected mare but was well held when third of six at Exeter (good) last month and almost certainly needs significant improvement.

Eighth foal; half-brother to six winners, one useful on the Flat in France and one useful over hurdles there; dam 1m 2yo winner, half-sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Lady Deauville; stable has fair bumper record; market may guide.

First foal from a French 2m4f/2m5f chase winner; ran well to a point but dropped out rather tamely and was beaten about 24l when eighth of 11 at Hereford (good) last month; needs that run to have brought him on.
Out of a French hurdle/chase winner; only fifth of seven in a point bumper last month and probably faces much stronger opposition here.
Attracted some market support but was last of the nine finishers on debut at Newton Abbot (good) last month; tongue-tie added.
50,000euros 3yo; third foal; half-brother to fair hurdler Ip Up; dam French hurdle/chase winner, half-sister to high-class cross-country chaser Easysland; stable has occasional bumper winners.

24,000euros 3yo; seventh foal; half-brother to fair hurdler/chaser Quick Sharpener and a point winner; dam unraced half-sister to hurdle/chase winner Off The Charts; stable does pretty well in bumpers.

Sixth foal; closely related to useful winners Guard Your Dreams (2m-2m4f hurdle/chase) and Carys' Commodity (2m3f-2m6f hurdle/chase); dam unraced half-sister to useful bumper/jumps winner The Jigsaw Man; with a top stable; must be considered.
Out of a half-sister to stable's smart bumper performer Commanche Red; last of five over C&D (soft) on debut two months ago; today's faster ground needs to show him in a much better light.
Out of a half-sister to stable's smart hurdler Ch'tibello and a smart French Flat racer; bought for presence felt.
